summary: kbCommit is the one sanctioned path for putting the notebook into git: it pathspec-stages and commits ONLY `.raw/` (the append-only source-of-truth logs), `okf.yaml`, and the notebook's own `.gitignore`, deliberately excluding the derived `notes/*.md` renders (gitignored, never publishable) and `.metrics/`. The pathspec'd `git commit -m msg -- <paths>` commits just those paths even when other work is staged, leaving that other staged work untouched. If the whole notebook is gitignored (a repo that opted out of sharing notes, as this repo's root .gitignore did until this session), `git add` fails with "ignored by one of your .gitignore" or "did not match any files" — kbCommit treats both as normal and returns kind:'nothing' rather than force-adding past the ignore rule.
